# YM12: 长春仙馆 Changchun Xianguan, "The Long Spring Lodge of the Immortal"

Wave 2 · Yuanming Yuan · 3D: `/reconstruction/3d.html?b=YM12` · Page: `/scenes/#YM12` · Row: `research/buildings/YM12-changchun-xianguan/`

## What it was

长春仙馆 Changchun Xianguan, south of 茹古涵今, on the west side of the front lake behind 正大光明: a three-bay gate, a five-bay main hall, 绿荫轩 Lüyin Xuan behind it and 丽景轩 Lijing Xuan behind the west gallery (S05 j81:5a); west of it 含碧堂 Hanbi Tang of five bays with 林虚桂静, 古香斋, 抑斋, 墨池云 and 随安室 (E1405, S05). It was Hongli's residence as a prince from 1729; after 1735 his empress used it and the dowager stayed here at festivals; Jiaqing lived here from 1796 under the retired Qianlong (E1406, E1411, S360). It gave its name to 长春园 (E1417, S02 p.98). Burned October 1860 (S02 pp.187-188).

From the inventory row: **built** 不晚于雍正四年 1726, 初名莲花馆 (S42;S43); by 1726, as 莲花馆; **destroyed** 1860 (S05, S02, S08, S42, S43, S01, S340).

## The scene itself

### The leaf of 1744, its poem and preface

Preface of 1744: "循壽山口西入屋宇深䆳重廊曲檻逶迤相接" (S05 j81:5b): entered west through the pass of 寿山, deep halls linked by double galleries and winding rails, a court with paulownias and rocks; 'my old residence, now slightly repaired, where I receive the Empress Dowager on festivals'.

### How later sources differ

Many later names: 丽景轩, 林虚桂静, 绿荫轩, 春好轩 Chunhao Xuan, 藤影花丛 Tengying Huacong all have poems by Jiaqing from 1796 (E1412-E1416, S360), when he lodged here. On S01 the five-bay main hall is labelled 藤影花丛 (YM12-02) and a seven-bay row carries the label 长春仙馆 (YM12-N01): the plan state is post-1796 and may have moved the name to another hall. 古香斋 was named after the east room of 重华宫 (E1407).

## Interior and setting

### Interior

Nothing written yet.

### The garden around it

Paulownias and rocks in the court (S05 j81:5b); magnolias at 含碧堂 (note of 1797, E1408); a stream 鸣玉溪 with a bridge pavilion (YM12-11, 卷棚歇山 per S41) and boating (E1409).
